newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Douwe Egberts to raise retail coffee price.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Douwe Egberts to raise retail coffee price.

text.p: Dutch coffee roaster Douwe Egberts said on Monday it would be raising the retail price of its coffee in response to the sharp rise in world prices.
A spokesman for the company told Reuters the company would be increasing the price of a 250-gramme pack of coffee by 25 cents, making an average retail price three guilders 55 cents.

"We have made the decision because of the higher structural price of coffee on the world market and because of the effects of the dollar," spokesman Joost den Haan said. He said the announcement had been made to the coffee trade today.
On January 24 Douwe Egberts, which holds 70 percent of the Dutch retail coffee market, said it was monitoring the situation very closely.
Coffee futures, the benchmark for world physical prices, have risen by around 30 percent this year on increasing fears of tight supplies as producers club together to restrict exports.
The Fair Trade Organisation also said on Monday it would be raising the retail price of its coffee by 25 cents on each 250 gramme pack. The group holds around one percent of the market.
